continuities.name: Avatarverse (animated canon)
continuities.description: The animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender and The Legend of Korra, their sequel comics, the Chronicles of the Avatar novels, the 2026 film Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender and Avatar: Seven Havens. Avatar calendar: years after (AG) / before (BG) the Air Nomad Genocide; BG stored as negative numbers (296 BG = -296). Absolute years come from the Avatar Wiki timeline (fan wiki), so they are inferred.
continuities.quote: A sequel animated series to ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'', ''The Legend of Korra'', ran from 2012 to 2014. The storylines of both animated series have been continued in comic book form. … [Avatar Aang] A continuation of the animated television series ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' (2005–2008) … [Seven Havens] It serves as a sequel series to ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' (2005–2008) and ''The Legend of Korra'' (2012–2014).

continuities.name: Dragon Ball main continuity
continuities.description: Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z (and its re-edit Kai), Daima, Super, and the four Toriyama-involved films (Battle of Gods, Resurrection 'F', Broly, Super Hero). Age calendar ("Age 749"); years from the Dragon Ball Wiki timeline (fan wiki, compiled from guidebooks and games), so inferred. Stored as plain numbers (Age 749 = 749).
continuities.quote: Dragon Ball (1986–89), Dragon Ball Z (1989–96), Dragon Ball Super (2015–18) and Dragon Ball Daima (2024–25) are set in a uniform main continuity,[citation needed] … Battle of Gods and Resurrection 'F' were remade into the first and second arcs of the Dragon Ball Super anime, which told the same stories as the two films in expanded detail. … Two sequel films were released: Broly (2018) and Super Hero (2022).

calendar.name: Age
calendar.epoch_note: Dragon Ball Wiki: "The following timeline is compiled using the years given in the guidebooks and video games"

continuities.note: The Wikipedia continuity sentence carries a [citation needed] tag (September 2026).

continuities.name: Dragon Ball GT (alternate continuity)
continuities.description: Anime-only sequel to Z. Treated as its own continuity because Super/Daima continue from Z instead. Age calendar ("Age 749"); years from the Dragon Ball Wiki timeline (fan wiki, compiled from guidebooks and games), so inferred. Stored as plain numbers (Age 749 = 749).
continuities.quote: … while Dragon Ball GT (1996–97) and Super Dragon Ball Heroes (2018–24) explore several alternate continuities.[citation needed] … [GT article] Chronologically, it is the last Dragon Ball series (taking place after Dragon Ball Z) and until the release of Dragon Ball Super (2015–2018), GT was the final televised series of the original Dragon Ball anime trilogy.
continuities.note: Wikipedia does not say in so many words that Super "supersedes" GT; the Dragon Ball article calls GT an alternate continuity (citation needed), while the GT article only says it takes place after Z. Separate continuity is the default used; GT branches from the end of Z.

continuities.description: The 17 older animated films (Curse of the Blood Rubies to The Path to Power), mostly alternate retellings or side stories. Ordered by Japanese release.
